verses.text: On another day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came with them to stand before the LORD.
The LORD asked Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered, "From roaming back and forth across the earth and walking all over it."

The LORD said, "Have you paid attention to my servant Job? There's no one like him on earth. He's blameless and upright, reveres God, and turns away from evil. He still holds on to his integrity, even though you urged me to ruin him for no reason."
Satan answered the LORD, "Skin for skin! A person will give up everything to save their own life.
Reach out now and strike his bones and flesh, and he'll turn against you to your face."
The LORD told Satan, "He's in your power. Spare his life."
Satan left the LORD's presence and struck Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.
Job picked up a piece of broken pottery to scrape his skin while he sat in the ashes.
His wife asked him, "Are you still holding on to your integrity? Renounce God and die."
Job told her, "You're talking like a foolish woman. Should we accept good from God and refuse to accept trouble?" Through all this, Job said nothing sinful.

When Job's three friends heard about the disasters that had come upon him, they each set out from home. Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite agreed to go together to share his grief and comfort him.
When they saw him from a distance, they barely recognized him. They wept aloud, tore their robes, and threw dust into the air over their heads.
They sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him because they could see how deeply he was suffering.
